title: Mantle Geodynamics
description: The mantle is solid rock, and yet it flows: a centimetre a year, heated from below, cooled from above, turning over like a pot on a stove. Its minerals - ringwoodite, bridgmanite - only exist under its pressure.

puzzle.goal: A layer of thickness L is heated from below by a temperature difference ΔT. Whether it turns over depends on one number: buoyancy (ρ g α ΔT) against heat diffusion κ and viscosity μ. Write that number, N.
puzzle.name: Rayleigh number
puzzle.form: ρ * g * α * T * L ^ 3 / ( κ * μ )
puzzle.expr: R * g * a * T * H ^ 3 / ( k * m )
puzzle.ask: Find N for the whole mantle: R = @{R} kg/m³, a = @{a} /K, T = @{T} K, H = @{H} m, k = @{k} m²/s, m = @{m} Pa·s.
puzzle.method: Compare how fast a warm blob rises (buoyancy over viscosity) with how fast it loses its heat (diffusion). Above about 1000 the layer convects.
